pullRequest.title: Disable automatic EEPROM updates for image-rota
pullRequest.body:
Summary

"image-rota" mounts "/boot/firmware" read-only, so "rpi-eeprom-update.service" cannot apply an update and can leave the system in a degraded state.

This change:

- gives "image-rota" a dedicated provider token
- makes "rpi-device-secpolicy" force "IGconf_rpisec_eepromupd=n" when that image type is present
- leaves EEPROM updates enabled by default for non-AB images
- extends the existing AB configuration dry-run test to verify the resolved policy

Fixes #270

nodes.diffHunk:
@@ -3,9 +3,9 @@
 # X-Env-Layer-Category: image
 # X-Env-Layer-Desc: Immutable GPT A/B layout for rotational OTA updates,
 #  boot/system redundancy, and a shared persistent data partition.
-# X-Env-Layer-Version: 6.0.0
+# X-Env-Layer-Version: 6.0.1
 # X-Env-Layer-Requires: image-base,device-base,rpi-ab-slot-mapper,systemd-min
-# X-Env-Layer-Provides: image
+# X-Env-Layer-Provides: image,image-rota

nodes.body:
The method and usage of a trigger to set this to `n` is exactly right, but making `rpi-device-secpolicy` aware of `image-rota` by name is a bad design choice because it hard-wires an implicit relationship between the two layers, rather than using (what would be better) a capability token.

I could envisage a `trait` being used for this instead. A suitable one would have to be thought about and created because right now, traits only describe hardware and boot time facts - not image generation characteristics.

I like the approach taken here, but it's not quite right.
nodes.diffHunk:
@@ -13,6 +13,8 @@
 # X-Env-Var-eepromupd-Required: n
 # X-Env-Var-eepromupd-Valid: bool
 # X-Env-Var-eepromupd-Set: y
+# X-Env-Var-eepromupd-Triggers:
+#  when=has('image-rota') set IGconf_rpisec_eepromupd=n policy=force

nodes.body:
We're on the right track but I think we need to re-type the trait token that's used. My suggestion first:

1. Remove `firmware-readonly` from `trait/boot/rpi/features.deb822`
2. Add new `trait/image.deb822` plus a new `trait/image/X.deb822` file holding a single token.
 
As here (no change), `image-rota` declares `Provides:` for the token and the secpolicy layer trigger uses the token to set `IGconf_rpisec_eepromupd=n`.

What the token is though, I don't know. Traits should be simple and generic where possible.

I kind of feel it should be `image:<something>:immutable` but as to what <something> is, I'm not sure.

I've recently changed the contents of the `image-rota` vfat boot partition so it now only contains boot.img (and an accompanying boot.sig when signed).  It's still mounted `ro` which makes even more sense now, particularly in the signed case.

I'm even wondering if we need a trait at all. If the `rpi-eeprom-update` systemd service itself had a conditional gate, it would handle it without needing to be disabled. For example:
```
# /etc/systemd/system/rpi-eeprom-update.service.d/read-only-trigger.conf
[Unit]
ConditionPathIsReadWrite=/boot/firmware
```
`image-rota` could drop that in today to prevent it starting, but what the drop-in couldn't tell is whether a particular update needs to write to the boot partition (or not). That depends on the hardware and on the image being installed, and only `rpi-eeprom-update` works it out.
